source_decisions.title: AI Server Demand Continues to Support Memory Prices in 3Q26, but Gains Moderate as Consumer Demand Weakens and High Base Effects Take Hold, Says TrendForce
source_decisions.reason: Publication is before cutoff and no later update is indicated; no separate revision timestamp was exposed.

observations.observation: On Sep. 30, TrendForce publicly forecast 4Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices +10–15% QoQ and NAND Flash +15–20% QoQ. It said enterprise SSDs were the only category expected to accelerate price growth, citing AI/CSP demand and constrained server-oriented supply.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are forecasts, not realized contract prices or Micron-specific results. The release also reports weak consumer demand, limited client SSD buying, and LTA pricing mechanisms that may cause some supplier increases to lag.

observations.observation: TrendForce’s July 3 prior 3Q26 forecast was +13–18% QoQ for conventional DRAM and +10–15% for NAND. Compared with those forecast bands, the Sep. 30 4Q forecast has conventional DRAM endpoints 3 percentage points lower and NAND endpoints 5 points higher; this is a comparison of forecasts, not actual price changes.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: Quarterly ranges are not directly comparable to realized prices, company-level ASPs, volumes, or margins.

observations.observation: TrendForce’s Sep. 23 DRAM bulletin is the earliest traceable public signal found that the 4Q26 DRAM contract-price outlook had been raised. The Sep. 24 forecast page then described AI/CSP-led demand and weak consumer demand, and gave an enterprise SSD forecast of +23–28% QoQ with overall NAND +15–20%.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The Sep. 23 public abstract does not expose the revised DRAM range, and the Sep. 24 displayed abstract does not state the conventional DRAM range; the detailed report is gated.

observations.observation: The primary release’s counterevidence is concentrated in consumer-facing segments: notebook costs weigh on sales, PC brands reduce mainstream SSD capacities, client SSD procurement is limited, and NAND wafer buyers are cautious. TrendForce also says LTA pricing terms can limit some server DRAM suppliers’ increases.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is counterevidence within the same TrendForce release, not independent corroboration. No company-specific Micron impact is established.
